items.title: Sauron Wears the One Ring and Battles the Balrog in New Rings of Power Season 3 Trailer
items.description: Prime Video has released a new trailer for the upcoming third season of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power that revealed more of the war to stop Sauron from forging the One Ring.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Prime Video has released a new trailer for the upcoming third season of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power that revealed more of the war to stop Sauron from forging the One Ring. You can watch the trailer via the player above or the embed below.

Season 3 is set several years after the events depicted in Season 2, picking up the story at the height of the War of the Elves.

While the new trailer features more looks at the Nazgnagôl, a Mûmakil, and fell beasts, the best is saved until last when Sauron dons the One Ring, which will allow him to bind all the peoples of Middle-earth to his will.

“I see the path to victory so certain,” Sauron says. “I will take my place as a conqueror, a sorcerer. A king. We have work to do.” These lines are spoken over footage of a Nazgnagôl getting the upper hand of Galadriel in a fight. (Sauron also seems to be getting into Galadriel’s head at one point as she dreams that he’s lying in bed next to her.)

It also appears Sauron will battle the Balrog at some point this season as the trailer shows a fiery battle. (Simon Pegg voices the Balrog in the show.)

After the death of Celebrimbor in the Rings of Power Season 2 finale, Sauron is still seeking to forge the One Ring to rule them all as Season 3 begins. It would seem this season is going to see the Dark Lord come out on top in his quest to bring Middle-earth under his rule – well, for now anyway.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 debuts on Prime Video on November 11. In the meantime, read up on the show’s mysterious new orc character and learn why the Harfoots won’t be in Season 3.

And also be sure to read our The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 2 finale review and our spoiler-filled Season 2 ending explained and how it sets up Season 3.

items.title: The Internet Reacts to the Cancellation of Mass Effect 5 and the Death of BioWare
items.description: The Internet Reacts to the Cancelation of Mass Effect 5 and the Death of BioWare.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
On October 21, EA announced a major restructuring of its development studios and current projects, which included the closure of BioWare and the cancellation of the next Mass Effect game.

This news hit fans like a truck, as many were excitedly waiting for the next installment in the beloved sci-fi role-playing series. BioWare created some of the most beloved and influential RPGs in history over the course of 30 years of existence, but its closure was relegated to just a single paragraph in EA's memo to staff on today's dramatic company changes.

“As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly,” Cam Weber, president and chief studios officer, and David Tinson, president and COO, said in the memo.

Needless to say, fans of BioWare games — particularly Mass Effect — were left devastated by this news. On social media, the prevailing sentiment seems to be one of anger and despair, with commenters venting their spleen at EA and the current state of the industry.

“I was so excited for N7 day. I was so excited for the next Mass Effect game. The Mass Effect trilogy is one of my favorite games of all time, and now it’s dead forever. I don’t even know what to think or say, everything feels unreal,” one fan wrote online.

“This is a f**king dagger in my heart. Thank you for being a huge part of my childhood,” another said.

“Please God, PLEASE sell your IPs to another company,” yet another urged. “Don't let the legacy of Mass Effect and Dragon Age die with these last gory gasps. Sell them to other companies that can continue telling the stories they can... Don't let EA hold these settings hostage.”

Prominent members of the video game development community also offered their thoughts. The co-CEO of The Witcher and Cyberpunk developer CD Projekt Red, Michal Nowakowski, weighed in with a statement honoring BioWare for its help and collaboration over the years.

“BioWare has been a massive part of CDPR history. We befriended them when localizing and selling Baldur’s Gate games in Poland, Czech, and Slovakia. And later, they were a great help when lending us their engine for Witcher 1, sharing their wisdom and even giving us a spot at their booth at E3. I had the pleasure to visit them a few times in Edmonton and also host them in our Warsaw office. Very sad for the people affected, but also sad to see a legendary brand go down. Not a great day in the games industry,” he wrote.

Paweł Sasko, associate game director on Cyberpunk 2, said BioWare's Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 "shaped my imagination and the desire to create games." He continued: "I would have never been here without BioWare igniting the fire in my heart. It inspired me, formed me, enriched my imagination, and for that I will be forever grateful. I will always remember you."

inXile boss Brian Fargo, who founded Interplay Entertainment, called it a "sad day indeed." "I remember when BioWare was a small studio that made Shattered Steel for us at Interplay," he said. "We saw the promise in what they could do, and they went on to create Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 and become legendary. A sad day indeed. My thoughts are with everyone there today."

Thomas Puha, communications director at Alan Wake and Control developer Remedy, commented: "This was coming but so sad to read. The growing problem for large publishers is that smaller AAA games won’t bring enough money so can’t take the risk on them, but not doing original games? We need those, need new franchises."

BioWare issued a statement of its own on social media, writing: “For more than 30 years, BioWare has been more than a studio. It has been a home for storytellers, developers, and the players who brought our worlds to life. Now, after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending.

“There is nothing easy about writing those words. Our focus right now is on our incredibly talented team who put their hearts into these games, and supporting one another through this transition. What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember. These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with the characters, and made these worlds your own. From all of us at BioWare, thank you for being the most meaningful part of our story.”

Mike Gamble, executive producer of Mass Effect at BioWare, told fans in a social media post: "Your support has meant everything to me over the past 17 years at BioWare."

It’s been a tumultuous year for EA; in August, the company went private in a $55 billion acquisition to an investor group comprised of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners. The Financial Times reported that this deal hinged on the hope that AI would “significantly” cut EA’s operating costs, helping the consortium of private investors to better manage the debt they piled onto the game company.

items.title: Glee Reboot Is Officially a Go at Disney+ and Hulu, and Gleeks Have Plenty of Thoughts
items.description: Disney+ and Hulu have officially picked up a series order of Ryan Murphy’s Glee reboot.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Disney+ and Hulu have officially picked up a series order of Ryan Murphy’s Glee reboot.

Murphy first revealed the possibility of a revival in July when he expressed his continued love for the musical series during an interview with People. By September, Murphy announced a finished script, alongside confirmation that he’s already spoken to “about 10 or so” original cast members about returning. While the series order announcement didn't initially reveal any casting news, original cast members like Lea Michele and Heather Morris have since confirmed their involvement.

Gleeks are reacting strongly to the news: “This is the best worst day of my life,” commented one fan. “This is gonna be so bad! I’m so happy and can’t wait,” said another.

Currently gleeking out! https://t.co/ckV50OCQ5s

— GLEE (@gleeofficial) October 21, 2026


Why the complicated feelings? Well, in the words of one dedicated Gleek account, “No one is more against this reboot than Gleeks because we all remember its excruciating devolution into insanity.”

While the early seasons of Glee were as critically acclaimed as they were popular, later seasons relied on shock plot lines while struggling to balance a rotating cast of characters. Murphy himself has developed quite the reputation for occasional tone deafness, most recently on display in the true crime Netflix series Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story, with an imagined ending that treats the serial killer series as some kind of MCU multiverse.

Fans’ primary concern, however? Whether we'll see a full reunion of the original cast. One fan argues that “a Glee revival with no cast announced is just a really expensive school choir.”

Some fans have particularly strong opinions on who exactly from the original cast is worth bringing back: “They need to go to Jane Lynch and offer her 1 billion dollars to return because thats the only way this is going to have a chance to work.” Lynch, who played the sardonic cheerleading coach Sue Sylvester, won an Emmy for the role in 2010.

The overwhelming majority of Gleeks have gathered in the comment sections of the announcement to pay tribute to the original cast members, arguing against bringing the series back without them. Per one fan, “Glee without Naya is like earth without water.” Rivera, who played fan-favorite Cheerio Santana Lopez, passed away in a tragic accident in 2020.

Fans also express concern over the reboot potentially “re-evaluating” some of the canon arcs from the original show, particularly the show’s groundbreaking queer relationships. “Don’t touch Brittana,” and “Don’t touch Klaine” are common refrains in the replies.

Still, some fans have a lot to gain from the show’s return. Popular X gimmick account Terri Schuester Updates, which has been consistently active since the show’s cancellation, was quick to recognize what this update means for their own career: “Wait, does this mean I might finally have some actual Terri Schuester updates?”

Other fans are already theorizing about what music will make its way into the reboot, pitching recent breakout popstars like Olivia Rodrigo and Chappell Roan. One particularly popular post jokingly takes a more simplistic stance on the reboot as a whole: “We’re about to get soooo many more songs to say 'they sang this on Glee' to, and that’s really what life is all about.”

Will that be enough reason for fans to tune into the reboot on Disney+? We’ll have to wait and see.

items.title: EA Sports Confirms It's Developing an Open-World Football Game
items.description: EA Sports is working on a new open-world football game, seemingly separate from Madden and College Football.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
EA Sports is working on a new open-world football game, seemingly separate from Madden and College Football.

In a new letter about EA's future, the company outlined what's on the horizon for its different portfolios. For its sports games, the publisher reaffirmed that it is working on a brand new Fight Night game, which will be EA's first boxing game in well over a decade. However, the more interesting announcement is that EA is working on a new open-world football game that it calls "Project Gridiron."

"We have two new projects in development you’ll hear about over the next few months, including a brand-new, social-first open-world experience for our American Football team that we call 'Project Gridiron,'" said EA. "And we are also in pre-production to bring back a beloved, fan-favorite in Fight Night, leveraging capabilities from our simulation fighting team."

It's unclear if Project Gridiron will have some kind of narrative or if its open-world will be a shared online universe, not unlike NBA 2K. Could this be a more mature and gritty football game, similar to what Fight Night Champion did for that series? It's hard to say right now. Madden briefly dabbled with narrative-driven campaigns in the mid to late 2010s with decent results, but eventually turned its focus back toward a broader career mode for those looking for a progressive single-player experience.

While a new College Football is expected to release next year per previous statements from EA Sports, the existence of Project Gridiron creates a question over whether or not Madden will be benched in favor of this new game.

After all, does anyone have the time, money, or interest in three EA-developed football games in a single year? It's also possible this is a total transformation of the Madden experience, but it sounds like something brand new. It sounds like we won't have to wait too long, as EA noted we will learn more about the game in the "next few months." Perhaps we'll hear about this during The Game Awards or sometime in early 2027, but we'll just have to wait and see.

A recent report also noted that there was some internal concern over the future of College Football, as the rising costs for NIL rights, in addition to other licensing and development expenses, are creating friction. The series' sales have reportedly declined year by year, leading some developers to worry the franchise's return may be relatively short-lived. Perhaps Project Gridiron could replace College Football in the future.

items.title: Xbox Insiders Can Now Stream Games by Buying Cloud Playtime Without Game Pass, Introductory Launch Pricing Revealed
items.description: Microsoft is now letting Xbox Insiders stream games by buying cloud playtime without a Game Pass subscription. Here's how much it costs.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Microsoft is now letting Xbox Insiders stream games by buying cloud playtime without a Game Pass subscription.

This preview is designed to give Insiders an early look at the new option before it rolls out more broadly next month. Insiders can buy cloud playtime, stream games on supported devices, and share feedback to help us continue improving the experience.

Cloud playtime is available to Insiders at introductory launch pricing:

  • 10hrs for $3.99
  • 25hrs for $7.99
  • 50hrs for $11.99

These cloud playtime packs let you play ad-free, and include shorter wait times, high-quality streaming, and playtime that remains available until it's used, Microsoft said. Insiders can also try cloud gaming for free with ads, as another option for accessing cloud gaming without a Game Pass subscription.

The cloud gaming options for Game Pass subscribers Microsoft announced last month are still set for November. From next month, Game Pass plans will include a set number of cloud gaming hours each month:

Xbox Game Pass cloud gaming monthly limits:

  • Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours
  • Game Pass Premium: 10 hours
  • Game Pass Essential: 5 hours

Once subscribers use their included hours, they can buy additional cloud playtime through the Xbox Store. Currently, Game Pass subscribers can stream without these monthly hour limits. The change means those who use cloud gaming most via Game Pass will end up having to pay more, although Microsoft said this impacts 4% of Game Pass subscribers.

Cloud gaming has become a focus as the RAMpocalypse makes console gaming increasingly expensive. Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, recently predicted the video game industry will be in “commercial streaming mode” within three years — but for video game streaming to matter, it would have to run GTA 6 just as well as consoles do.

During an investor focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, Zelnick was asked for his thoughts on the video game industry as it buckles under the pressure of skyrocketing chip costs, which have forced Sony and Microsoft to raise the price of their consoles and potentially delay the launches of the PlayStation 6 and the next-gen Xbox, codenamed Project Helix.

Zelnick admitted the rising cost of hardware “is not a good thing,” because cheaper hardware means more hardware in people’s hands, which is what software companies desire. But he suggested the advent of video game streaming would go a long way to tackling this problem.

Both Sony and Microsoft are predicted to lean heavily on streaming in the coming years as they contend with the RAMpocalypse. “I just don't have any insight as to what the console manufacturers have planned, but it wouldn't at all surprise me if part of what they plan is streaming,” Zelnick offered.

Just this week, it was reported that the next-gen Xbox may cost as much as $1,800, with a new handheld rumored for next year. New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said the spiralling cost of new and existing consoles would require "radically different business models" over the coming generation. She added that the industry had "reached a point where it will be hard to imagine" mass audiences still being able to afford "thousands of dollars" for a new console generation.

The current PS5 and Xbox Series X and S generation of consoles have seen price increases rather than cost savings. Sony itself raised the price of PS5 consoles back in March, blaming “continued pressures in the global economic landscape.” Nintendo has also not been immune, and recently acknowledged it would up the price of Switch 2, just over a year after its arrival. And Valve has bemoaned its struggle to release Steam Machine at the price it had initially hoped, instead having to go for an eye-watering $1,049.

And Valve has bemoaned its struggle to release Steam Machine at the price it had initially hoped, instead having to go for an eye-watering $1,049.

items.title: Diablo Is Getting a New Board Game Adaptation You Can Play Solo or With Friends
items.author: Jacob Kienlen
items.content:
Announced today, Glass Cannon Unplugged, the same studio behind tabletop adaptations of Don’t Starve, Dying Light, and Apex Legends among others, are getting ready to take on the demons of Sanctuary with Diablo: Unbound. Launching a campaign over on Gamefound, Diablo: Unbound is a cooperative dungeon battler for between 1-4 players and features iconic locations and beasts as you level up, and gear out a champion from familiar classes like the Rogue and Barbarian in a quest to take down the dungeon boss.

Diablo®: Unbound is a co-op dungeon battler for 1–4 players. Choose your Class, Dungeon, enemies, and Boss. Fight hordes, hunt loot, and grow stronger!

Follow on Gamefound to claim your free, Gamefound Exclusive Treasure Goblin Expansion

Launching Q1 2027.

#boardgames #diablo https://t.co/jZbqbVd4ze

— Glass Cannon Unplugged (@GCUtabletop) October 21, 2026

Details are still fairly scarce but already just in the trailer we get some exciting looks at the game from some awesome looking miniatures, various player boards, and even an idea of what the character systems might be. Judging by the map, Unbound looks to have you and your allies facing off against hordes of monsters on a hex grid.

As a big fan of deck builders, seeing that your special abilities and actions are tied to a deck of sorts, has me intrigued. The trailer also showcases a glimpse at the player boards with spots allocated for various armor pieces (with spots open even for gems) including chest, a left and right weapon slot, helm, ring, and necklace. Skills also appear to be taking a page out of the Slay the Spire board game rulebook with skill cards being double-sided with a base side and upgraded side so prepare for sleeving cards, folks.

At a quick glance, fans of boss battlers and dungeon crawling board games, Diablo: Unbound should take notice as this is already teasing some neat systems. For those attending the massive board game convention in Germany, Spiel Essen, this week, you can try out an early build of the game at the Glass Cannon Unplugged booth in Hall I with the campaign planned to launch in Q1 of 2027.

If you're interested in more board games you can play solo, make sure to check out IGN's list of the best single-player tabletop games available now.

items.title: WoW Forever Beta Extended to Friday, Name Reservations Go Live Tuesday
items.description: The World of Warcraft Forever beta has been incredibly popular, but just like any other beta, it has to come to an end as the full launch approaches. But Blizzard has extended the beta by a couple of days.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
The World of Warcraft Forever beta has been incredibly popular, but just like any other, it has to come to an end as the full launch approaches. Thankfully, Blizzard has extended the beta by a couple of days.

WoW Forever's beta was supposed to end yesterday, October 20, but Blizzard announced on X/Twitter that it would be extending the experience by three days. Now the beta will end on October 23 at 10am PT / 1pm ET. After it ends, Blizzard will open name reservations on October 27, which will let you reserve names for three different characters – just make sure they don't break the rules.

It's easy to forget that WoW Forever isn't just out already. Since the beta went live in September, people have been playing it constantly, and just among people playing the beta, there have already been a million characters made. Blizzard devs have even come out and said they were surprised by how many people flocked to the temporary test version of the Classic+ game mode.

Once the full game comes out on November 4, all you'll need to play WoW: Forever is an active subscription or a friend code (though that will just be temporary), so it'll likely be even more popular.

Fans have loved how true the content in the beta so far has stayed to the spirit of the early days of World of Warcraft. Blizzard has made it a point to avoid adding some modern quality-of-life improvements like shared tagging in order to maintain that classic feel. But, rather than strictly avoiding adding anything that was added after WoW's expansions started coming out, Blizzard has included content like the beloved 'Kyle's Gone Missing' quest that takes place in Mulgore.

There have been controversies, too, of course – it wouldn't be WoW without them. Blizzard has had to crack down hard on gold selling, and the company has also been strict with character names. We've even seen people griefing other players by putting down campfires where new players spawn so they die before the intro cinematic finishes.

If you haven't had a chance to dive into the beta yet, you still have a couple days to do so. But keep in mind that any progress you make will be deleted when the game launches in a couple of weeks.

items.title: EA Confirms DICE and Respawn Are Collaborating on a New Project Amidst Star Wars: Battlefront 3 Rumors
items.description: EA has confirmed that DICE and Respawn are working on a new project together, adding more fuel to rumors about Star Wars: Battlefront 3.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
EA has confirmed that DICE and Respawn are working on a new project together, adding more fuel to rumors about Star Wars: Battlefront 3.

As part of a larger letter about the future of EA, the publisher confirmed that it is working on new Battlefield games. It also noted that in addition to Battlefield, DICE and Respawn are working together on a "future project" that they hope will unlock growth in their shooter portfolio. This follows rumors from earlier this week that the two companies are working together to make Star Wars: Battlefront 3.

"In addition to our future Battlefield titles, we’ll be bringing together our Respawn and DICE studios to collaborate on a future project that will help us achieve that ambition," said EA. "We can’t wait to share more when the time comes."

Variety also corroborated the Battlefront 3 rumors via sources, though nothing was shared on what the game will look like or when it might release. Other rumors recently suggested that Bungie was in the mix to work on Battlefront 3 or perhaps another project in the Star Wars universe, though nothing has been confirmed on that front. Star Wars: Battlefront 3 has been one of the most demanded titles over the last decade.

DICE's second crack at the Star Wars shooter franchise was controversial at launch due to issues with its monetization strategy, but the game itself was praised up and down by fans. It has remained a respected title among Star Wars lovers, and they've frequently rallied together to demand a sequel. Now, it seems like it will happen, though this time with the assistance of Respawn.

The Titanfall and Apex Legends studio has its own experience working on Star Wars through the Jedi games and the recently-released Star Wars Zero Company. Respawn also worked on a canceled Star Wars shooter, rumored to be a Mandalorian game, leaving fans to wonder what could've been. Only time will tell what this new Respawn and DICE game really is, but if it's Battlefront 3, it has serious potential to be something special.

This news came alongside some doom and gloom. EA confirmed that it was canceling the next Mass Effect and shutting down veteran RPG studio BioWare. The news comes after about a decade of commercial and critical misfires from the studio with games like Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard.

items.title: Anime Characters Dominate Top Trending Pet Names of 2026
items.description: The top-trending dog and cat names in the United States are dominated by anime characters from franchises such as KPop Demon Hunters and Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
The top-trending dog and cat names in the United States are dominated by anime characters from franchises such as KPop Demon Hunters and Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle. Characters from The Odyssey and Star Wars: Andor also made the cut.

Names derived from movies and TV shows were the third highest trend in US pet names behind the categories of cottagecore and vintage revival, according to Rover.

The site reveals the top two trending dog names of 2026 are Rumi (KPop Demon Hunters) and Lumi (Lumi and the Great Big Galaxy).

Among dogs, Rover’s top trending movie/TV pet names are Telemachus (The Odyssey), Kleya (Andor), Heathcliff (Wuthering Heights), Fiyero (Wicked: For Good) and Jinu (KPop Demon Hunters).

The top five trending names for cats are Giyu (Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle), Shinobu (Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle), Jinu (KPop Demon Hunters), Derpy (KPop Demon Hunters), and Nessa (Wicked: For Good).

“New names inspired by the big screen this year include Dek (from Predator: Badlands), Reze (from Chainsaw Man: Reze Arc) and Slurp (from Wednesday) for dogs. New for cats are Kamek (from The Super Mario Bros. Movie), Kleya (from Andor) and Makima (from Chainsaw Man: Reze Arc),” according to Rover.

For more anime coverage, find out the latest on the KPop Demon Hunters movie sequel and read up on why Obsession star Inde Navarrette studied Jujutsu Kaisen and Demon Slayer to learn screenwriting.

What’s your pet’s name? Let us know in the comments.

items.title: BioWare Shutting Down, Next Mass Effect Canceled
items.description: BioWare is shutting down and the next Mass Effect game is canceled, according to a new report.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
BioWare is shutting down and the next Mass Effect game is canceled, EA has announced.

Bloomberg said BioWare closes its doors amid mass layoffs at Electronic Arts, which amount to 400 people losing their jobs (approx. 3% of total staff). Roughly 50 of these roles were at BioWare.

After the franchise-best sales of Dragon Age: Inquisition, BioWare sought live-service success with Anthem, then spent the best part of a decade on the troubled Dragon Age: The Veilguard. Both underperformed. Mass Effect, meanwhile, has seen mixed success. Mass Effect Andromeda is widely considered a disappointment among fans, though the series' more recent Legendary Edition remaster was well-received.

BioWare had spent the past half a decade gradual teasing the next Mass Effect's setting and story. We'd had it confirmed that Mass Effect 5 would have been set hundreds of years after Mass Effect 3, and feature a narrative that re-centers the action on the franchise's original Milky Way setting, long after the Reapers were defeated. Now, fans will never find out what happens next.

It is unclear what this means for Amazon's live-action Mass Effect series, which was also meant to be set after the events of Mass Effect 3 and tell a fresh story. Earlier this year, Mass Effect TV series co-showrunner Daniel Casey refuted a report that suggested the upcoming adaptation had recently undergone rewrites to be "more appealing to non-gamers."

EA will continue with sports games, Respawn's Apex Legends, action-adventure games (Star Wars: Jedi 3 and Marvel's Iron Man), and Battlefield. Bloomberg said Respawn and DICE are likely working on Star Wars: Battlefront 3, as had been rumored.

The drastic cuts come just a few months after EA went private in a leveraged buyout worth $55 billion, backed in large part by the Saudi Public Investment Fund, as well as the U.S. private equity firm Silver lake and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners.

In a memo sent to staff today, Cam Weber, president and chief studios officer, and David Tinson, president and COO, described itself as "the number one publisher in Western HD gaming, but "our industry is changing quickly."

"Players have more choices than ever for their time and attention, competition is intensifying, and some of our biggest opportunities for growth are beyond the markets, platforms, and business models where EA has traditionally been the strongest," they said.

EA reacted to this by "concentrating our teams, technology, and investment" behind three strategic priorities: "Deepen Our Core; "Expand Our Reach;" and "Transform Our Business."

"Our greatest opportunity starts with our franchises and global communities that have made EA a leader in interactive entertainment," the pair continued. "This is where we’ve had to make our hardest choices. Saying no to some things we're passionate about allows us to focus our teams and resources so we give our biggest opportunities everything they need to succeed."

Last year's Battlefield 6 was a "great success." Future Battlefield games are on the way, as well as the Respawn and DICE collaboration project that is believed to be Star Wars: Battlefront 3. EA said it will also continue to "invest heavily" in Respawn's battle royale, Apex Legends, over the next few years by introducing brand new gameplay modes in multiplayer, and "other new experiences, to expand the universe."

Marvel’s Iron Man (EA Motive) and the next Star Wars Jedi 3 (Respawn) live on, but expect "fewer simultaneous, large-scale projects," in the action-adventure genre from EA. And here's the official blurb on the end of BioWare and Mass Effect:

As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly.

EA Sports will of course continue the FC franchise. Two new projects are in development which are due to be revealed in the next few months: "a brand-new, social-first open-world experience for our American Football team that we call 'Project Gridiron,' and we are also in pre-production to bring back a beloved, fan-favorite in Fight Night, leveraging capabilities from our simulation fighting team."

The "Lifestyle," category, as EA calls it, will see Project Evergreen continue but Project Lotus paused. Both are The Sims projects. Skate, meanwhile, had "a lot of success in bringing players into the game, and we need to create an experience that keeps them engaged over the long-term. To do that, we are making changes to the studio to have a more focused, smaller team to deliver on a very clear roadmap for our community that we believe will build a healthier and more sustainable business."

Less than 12 months ago, Mike Gamble, executive producer of Mass Effect at BioWare, celebrated N7 Day to say the next Mass Effect game was still in development, to express excitement about the Amazon TV series, and to insist EA and BioWare "remain committed to telling more stories in this universe."

In a social media post published today, Gamble told fans, "Your support has meant everything to me over the past 17 years at BioWare."

items.title: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ Players Are Losing Loot to Server Crashes Despite Official Fix from Infinity Ward
items.description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's new extraction mode, DMZ, is experiencing server issues, causing players to lose newly earned loot.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's new extraction mode, DMZ, is experiencing server issues, causing players to lose newly earned loot.

Yesterday, Infinity Ward put its new extraction mode into early access ahead of MW4's full release on Friday. It's giving players a chance to mess around with the game's other offerings before the main course is unleashed, and while the reception has been glowing so far, there are some issues. The game's been having server crashes, casuing to players lose any loot they picked up.

Thankfully, any loot that you already extracted to the FOB and brought back into the DMZ as part of a loadout is safe, but anything you picked up during the run that you were booted from is lost. Infinity Ward claims the matter has been fixed and has confirmed what players will keep and lose.

"Players who disconnected due to this particular issue will retain the equipment they started the match with and their subsequent progression, but not the loot collected during the match," devs said in an update on Twitter/X.

📢 Call of Duty: #ModernWarfare4 | #DMZ Early Access

We’re aware of an issue causing some players to disconnect from matches. We’ve deployed a potential fix and are monitoring the results.

Players who disconnected due to this particular issue will retain the equipment they started the match with and their subsequent progression, but not the loot collected during the match.

— Call of Duty Updates (@CODUpdates) October 21, 2026

Some players are still reporting problems, so your mileage may vary. Of course, it's difficult to ensure everything that a player had when they were booted is safe. If that were the case, it could theoretically be abused by players to extract valuable loot without having to actually find an extraction zone. Still, if you found something extremely rare or valuable and lost it due to technical issues, it would be extremely frustrating.

Black Ops 7's Endgame mode had similar issues when it launched last year. The PvE extraction mode encouraged players to grind for rewards, but if you died or failed to extract, you would lose everything. Unfortunately, that also applied to crashes during the game's first few days. This was eventually fixed, but it was an agonizing first impression for anyone who spent hours grinding the game, only for it to be undone by something out of your control.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's full release will hit on October 23. The game's acclaimed campaign and DMZ modes are available to play now for owners of the title.

items.title: Everything Coming to Cyberpunk 2077 With the 2.5 Update, Including New Side Quests, New Double Trouble Perk, and Much More
items.description: CD Projekt has revealed what to expect from the Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 update, which ties in with the release of Netflix anime Edgerunners 2. Check out the patch notes.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
CD Projekt has revealed what to expect from the Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 update, which ties in with the release of Netflix anime Edgerunners 2.

Edgerunners content includes a new side quest called Clampdown, which is set before the events of Edgerunners 2 (CD Projekt recently confirmed that Edgerunners 2 is set in 2078, just one year after the game itself). During this quest you’ll get a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King from Season 2. There’s also a new radio station that has tracks from the Edgerunners series.

But there’s plenty more coming with 2.5 unrelated to Edgerunners, including more side quests. The Welcome to Paradise! side quest takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night, the founder of Night City itself. There’s also a new side quest that acts as an extension of Fool on the Hill, which includes new tarot cards.

Meanwhile, 2.5 lets you customize your hand cyberware, which will let you give your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System implants a new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

Perhaps the most significant addition with 2.5 is the new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree, which lets you dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category for the first time. The hope is that the perk will enable an entirely new playstyle, and I’m sure fans will get a kick out of trying it out.

Elsewhere, there’s cross-platform mod support on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X and S, and various quality-of-life improvements, such as saves in the “Load Game” menu grouped by separate playthroughs, and, finally, an FOV (Field Of View) slider on consoles.

On the tech side of things, there’s support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model, and various performance improvements.

Overall, 2.5 is a welcome surprise for Cyberpunk 2077, after CD Projekt had indicated it had no plans for further DLC for the hugely successful game. Of course, The Witcher 3 is getting a new expansion 12 years after launch, so perhaps CD Projekt will return later on with a new expansion for Cyberpunk 2077. For now, though, 2.5 is sure to spark a return to Night City for lapsed players, and give fans of Edgerunners a push to jump in if they haven’t already.

Cyberpunk 2077 2.5 update patch notes:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.
  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.
  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:
  • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China
  • Jinguji: available in City Center
  • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown
  • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside
  • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...
  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.
  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.
  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.
  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.
  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.
  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.
  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

Mod the World

  • Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.
  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.
  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.
  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.
  • Added an FOV (Field Of View) slider on consoles.
  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.
  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.
  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.
  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation and Denoising on Mac.
  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.
  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing and for PlayStation 5 Pro.
  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

Fixes

  • Fixed an issue on Nintendo Switch 2 where saving the game could result in a "Save failed - insufficient space" error.
  • Fixed an issue where adjusting HDR settings on PlayStation 5 had no effect.
  • Things Done Changed - Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.
  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.
  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.
  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.
  • Fixed several typos in various languages.
  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

items.title: Exclusive — See 7 New Cards From Magic: The Gathering Star Trek, Including 1 That Remembers the Most Iconic Drink of TNG
items.description: Magic: The Gathering: Star Trek is the card game's final frontier of 2026, and while Wizards of the Coast revealed quite a few of the cards yesterday, IGN today has seven cards we can exclusively reveal ahead of the November 13 release date.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Magic: The Gathering: Star Trek is the card game's final frontier of 2026, and while Wizards of the Coast revealed quite a few of the cards yesterday, IGN today has seven cards we can exclusively reveal ahead of the November 13 release date.

Just like the Marvel Superheroes set that came out earlier this year, Magic: The Gathering Star Trek has cards from pretty much every era of the show's history. Even the small selection of cards we have here covers everything from the original series to Deep Space 9 and Lower Decks.

MTG Star Trek Exclusive Card Reveals

We're revealing seven exclusive Magic: The Gathering Star Trek cards:

  • Mirror Universe Invasion
  • Dahar master
  • Pure Energy
  • Tea, Earl Grey, Hot
  • Unexplored Territory
  • Vexing Drone
  • Warp Core

The star of the show is a common artifact called 'Tea, Earl Grey, Hot.' Really, the reason why this card is noteworthy is because of the reference to Captain Picard's hot beverage of choice, but in the right deck, it could do some work. It's simply a 2 mana artifact with the 'Food' subtype, which automatically makes it useful in some decks.

But unlike the Food Tokens we've all made hundreds of, this one nets you a card when it enters. When you sacrifice it, you can either gain 3 life like any other Food Token, or you can have it deal 2 damage to an opponent. Finally, I can just throw tea in someone's face.

The more mechanically interesting card is Mirror Universe Intrusion. It's a sorcery for a colorless, a blue and a black, that lets you create a copy of a creature an opponent controls, only it has menace. That's a flavor win, but something that you can do with countless other cards.

However, if you pay the kicker of 4 colorless, a blue and a black, you instead copy all of your opponent's creatures, and give them all menace. At nine mana, it's quite an investment, but a good way to essentially steal an opponent's board.

Mirror Universe Intrusion also has a couple of 'booster fun' treatments, with a borderless version and the new showcase treatment that loos like it came right out of a Star Trek box set.

Dahar Master is a 4-mana 4/3 at common, and with its ability to sacrifice a nonland permanant to shock any target, should be useful at your prerelease. But it's kind of one of those cards that's going to end up populating a bulk box the day after you open it in a pack.

Unexplored Wilds is interesting, becuase it's an effect we've seen countless times with cards like Evolving Wilds, but worse. You can tap it for a colorless mana, unlike Evolving Wilds, but if you want to sacrifice it to tutor up a basic land, you need to spend one mana to do it, which is bad. Just like Dahar Master, this will probably be useful in draft to help you color fix, but it's going to end up in your bulk box the moment you get home.

This new Star Trek set is shaping up to at least be the most interesting Universes Beyond set of the year so far, and I am interested to see how some of the artifact strategies play out across different formats. This set is also getting previewed after Wizards of the Coast revealed Darkhold Destiny at an NYCC panel, which takes a Universes Beyond property and creates a wholly original story.

media:description.$text:
Star Trek has been around for so long now that, for the purposes of a listicle like this, it seems only fair to group the franchise’s output by era. You’ve got The Original Series period of the late ’60s, then there’s the movies featuring those old scientists, which then gave way to the Rick Berman era which started with Next Generation and ended with Enterprise, and then of course there’s the modern era of Parmount+ shows which began with Discovery in 2017.

And that’s what we’re discussing today, as the service formerly known as CBS All Access (remember that?) launches the first straight-to-streaming TV movie, Star Trek: Section 31 (which actually originated as a series). In less than eight years, the modern Trek brain trust has also created five new shows, two of which are animated, as well as a series of shorts known as, of course, Short Treks.

With the variety of approaches that these different projects have taken on – from straight sci-fi drama to comedy, animation, shorts, feature-length, and more – comparing them to one another is a bit tricky. There’s also the fact that a show can have good and bad seasons, so keep that in mind when looking at our rankings as we’ve taken a series’ entire run into account rather than just focused on a favorite run of episodes.

So with all that said, let’s make it so, engage, fly, blast off, punch it, or whatever else is your favorite thing to say while cosplaying as a Starfleet captain!

items.title: Fallout Day Continues: The World of Fallout Museum Exhibit Expands, Choose the Flavor of Nuka Twist, and More
items.description: As part of the ongoing Fallout Day celebrations, Bethesda has revealed new Fallout partnerships in the real world.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
As part of the ongoing Fallout Day celebrations, Bethesda has revealed new Fallout partnerships in the real world.

The highlight for me is the expansion of the World of Fallout exhibit at the National Atomic Testing Museum in Las Vegas. This includes a collection of props, costumes, and memorabilia from the games and the Amazon TV show. The update will introduce two new galleries, doubling its footprint and featuring interactive installations, museum artifacts, and interpretive displays. Check out pictures of the exhibit in the slideshow below:

Across the globe, the Fallout Cafe returns to Tower Records in Tokyo for a second year, offering Fallout-themed food and exclusive merchandise. We’ve got images of what to expect if you can make your way to Japan for a visit. Images including of the menu are below:

Back on home soil, the third annual Fallout Night with the Texas Stars is set for October 24. Fans who attend can receive a collectible Fallout bobblehead.

And finally — and perhaps most importantly! — Bethesda and Jones Soda’s next collaboration is Project T.W.I.S.T. (Taste-worthiness Initiative for Shelter Transition), which invites fans to help choose the flavor of Nuka Twist. This is important because the flavor of Nuka Twist has not yet been established in game content. Voting takes place on the Jones Soda website October 21-31.

Nuka-Twist was added to Fallout 76 as a Nuka-Cola variant consumable as part of the Nuka-World on Tour update. Drinking it gets you a 10 minute, +2 buff of one of your 7 S.P.E.C.I.A.L. stats, so it’s pretty handy. Watch out for those +5 rads, though.

Already this week, Bethesda has shown off three eye-catching mods for Fallout 4, one of which launched yesterday, October 20. Fallout Day itself is this Friday, October 23 (October 23, 2077 is of course the day in the Fallout timeline the bombs fell, sparking The Great War that caused the irradiated wasteland fans of the franchise have been playing in over the last few decades).

Fallout’s 30th anniversary arrives next year, so expect some big announcements from Bethesda then. What’s it working on? It’s got everything from Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters to Fallout 5, with an Obsidian-developed Fallout spinoff in there somewhere. Work continues on Fallout 76 and Fallout Shelter, and Season 3 of the Fallout TV series is also incoming. In short, Microsoft is doubling down on Fallout, with new Xbox boss Asha Sharma striving for increased profitability.

items.title: First Permanent Pokémon Store Outside Asia to Open in London by 2029
items.description: The first permanent Pokémon store outside Asia will open in London “by 2029.”
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
The first permanent Pokémon store outside Asia will open in London “by 2029.” The retail space will be open to fans of all ages, with merchandise, community spaces, and “one-of-a-kind experiences.”

According to The Pokémon Company, the store’s opening will kick off a broader rollout of stores across the world. The exact location for the London store hasn’t been announced.

“We are always exploring new opportunities that help us create unique and memorable experiences for our fans,” chief product and experience Officer at The Pokémon Company International, Gaku Susai, said. “This new London store will give visitors the chance to step into the world of Pokémon, whether they’re discovering the brand for the first time or have been Trainers for years.

“We hope it becomes a place where everyone can come together, feel like part of a community and enjoy the magic of Pokémon in a whole new way.”

A previous location opened in New York in 2001, but was closed in 2005 to make way for Nintendo New York, a store with broader Nintendo-based merch. The London store doesn’t have a name yet, but The Pokémon Company avoided calling it a Pokémon Center in its announcement.

The store’s opening is part of a wider expansion by Pokémon in the UK. The Pokémon European International Championships, hosted at London’s Excel Center for the past several years, features its own pop-up Pokémon Center which always sells out fast.

items.title: Halo Special Edition Xbox Console Hallmark Keepsake Ornament Is Now Available
items.description: Hallmark has just released a delightful Keepsake Ornament based on the Halo Special Edition of the original Xbox console that Microsoft released in 2004.
items.author: Chris Reed
items.content:
Every year, Hallmark releases hundreds of new Christmas ornaments, including some very cool ones based on video games and geek culture. This year, as an Amazon-exclusive release that just went live, you can get the Xbox Halo Special Edition Console Hallmark Keepsake Ornament (see it at Amazon). The ornament is a miniature version of the translucent green Halo-themed special edition Xbox console Microsoft released in 2004. It’s available now for $27.99.

Xbox Halo Special Edition Console - Hallmark Keepsake Ornament

The ornament looks just like a tiny version of the real thing. It has the chunky rectangular console, decked out in translucent green plastic and the words “Halo Special Edition” on the front right. It also has an adorable little cord leading to a similarly green original Xbox controller sitting on the console.

It’s also a “Magic Light and Sound” ornament, meaning it, well, lights up and makes sound. When you press the tiny Power button on the ornament, the light comes on and it plays the console startup sound and music from "Halo Theme Mjolnir Mix" from Halo 2.

Also included are the three Alkaline LR44 button batteries required to make it light up and play music. And the size in inches is 3.5 x 1.25 x 3.5, so it's a small thing (you know, the size of a standard Christmas ornament). I have the SNES Hallmark Keepsake Ornament, and I love it.

Original Xbox Console Ornament

If you’re interested in an original Xbox Christmas ornament but you're not particularly keen on the Halo Special Edition, you can purchase a standard Xbox Hallmark Keepsake Ornament instead (see it at Amazon). It debuted in 2024 but is still available and still looks like a perfectly tiny version of Microsoft’s original game console.

More 2026 Hallmark Keepsake Ornaments

Alternately, a bunch more gaming ornaments came out this year, including a Halo Warthog, as well as Pokémon, Zelda, and more. Fans of other classic consoles can pick up a rather excellent PS1 ornament, perhaps to complement their PlayStation LEGO set?

In similar news, Microsoft is releasing a new translucent green version of the Xbox Series X on November 13. However, only 25,000 of these special edition consoles are being made, and it has already sold out everywhere it went up for preorder. You may be able to get one at release, if more stock becomes available.

items.title: CD Projekt's Cyberpunk 2077 Loremaster Confirms Year Edgerunners 2 Is Set, Sparking Fan Speculation About Canon Endings
items.description: CD Projekt Red loremaster Patrick Mills has revealed the exact year Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 takes place, amid speculation from fans about what it means for the ending of Cyberpunk 2077.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
CD Projekt Red loremaster Patrick Mills has revealed the exact year Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 takes place, amid speculation from fans about what it means for the ending of Cyberpunk 2077.

According to Mills, Season 2 takes place not long after you bite the bullet and finally meet Hanako at Embers in Cyberpunk 2077.

"Ok so the thing is that I am seeing a lot of people assuming S2 takes place before 2077 but it doesn't, it takes place in 2078," Mills confirmed in a post on Bluesky. "Moving things forward, time doesn't stop in Cyberpunk."

Mills previously posted about a misunderstanding he had seen in early reviews of the series, but wanted to wait until it was out before dropping a truth nuke.

In Edgerunners Season 2, powerful corporation Arasaka doesn’t quite have the same pull it did during the events of Cyberpunk 2077, which is a hint that the anime takes place after the events of the game. There are also some other smaller and bigger details, but like the loremaster, I don’t want to spoil things for you.

Now they know Edgerunners 2 is set just a year after the events of Cyberpunk 2077, fans are trying to work out what it means for the plot of the game. Some believe it suggests certain endings are canon. Or, perhaps it would be better to say, some believe it suggests certain endings are not canon. In truth, Edgerunners 2 doesn't force CD Projekt into making a decision about canon — a bit like Bethesda's position on Fallout canon in the context of the Amazon TV show, which takes place after all the video games.

The world of Cyberpunk is set to expand further, of course, with the in-development Cyberpunk 2 (where and when the game takes place is yet to be announced). There's also a live-action film in the works, although according to CD Projekt, the Cyberpunk 2077 movie won't retrace the game's steps.

Before all that, Cyberpunk 2077 is set for a surprise Edgerunners 2-themed update this week. CD Projekt has confirmed it features cyberware customization and a new dual-wielding playstyle. CDPR released a similar update to tie into the first season. The Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners update added a short questline that let players track down the cool yellow jacket the protagonist of Season 1 wore. There’s a good chance the new update will come with some similar surprises when it drops on October 22.

More details about the Edgerunners 2 update will be revealed today, October 21, 2026, during a special episode of REDstreams.

items.title: Crimson Desert Charting the Unknown DLC Features Revealed, Including Shipbuilding, Romance, and Housing
items.description: Pearl Abyss has pulled back the curtain on the upcoming Crimson Desert DLC, Charting the Unknown, revealing what players can expect. Here's a rundown of all the new features, systems, and mechanics.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Pearl Abyss has pulled back the curtain on the upcoming Crimson Desert DLC, Charting the Unknown, revealing what players can expect.

Charting the Unknown adds new stories, ocean exploration, romance, business management and expanded housing to an already feature-packed Pywel. We have everything you need to know about the major additions below.

The plot thickens…

There are character focused stories for playable characters Kliff, Damiane, and Oongka, who, having put the fight for the Greymanes and Pywell to bed, set out on new paths. They’ll encounter allies and threats “both old and new.” Based on the new overview video, these new individual character stories will be relatively involved, with cutscenes pushing the plot forward.

Ocean voyages and shipbuilding

The DLC expands the Great Ocean of Pywel area, which you might have crossed in the base game on the back of a dragon. After establishing the Greymane camp, you can unlock shipbuilding, then gather resources to build your own vessel and customize it before you set sail. Pearl Abyss said that you’ll fight enemies (there’s ship combat), establish new strongholds with the Greymanes, and earn new rewards.

You can craft your own dive suit to help you delve deeper into the ocean. “More secrets lie beneath the surface, where new underwater traversal methods let players dive below the waves to uncover sunken ruins, treasure and resources,” Pearl Abyss said, while showing off the ability to hitch a ride on the back of a sea creature.

Romance and marriage

If you earn the trust of certain characters you can develop romantic relationships and even marry, Pearl Abyss said. One potential romance option is Bari, the Witch of Kindness. Pictures shown reveal a number of dialogue options tied to this mechanic, including "Give a genuine compliment," and "Confess your feelings." “Close” companions may also visit the Greymane Camp to “spend some time together.”

Housing

As for housing, you will be able to design the structure of your home from the ground up, including the placement of walls, windows and other structural elements. This sounds fun: once you’ve liberated certain castles, you can claim them and decorate their interiors, turning it into a new home.

Business management

In the base game, once the Greymane camp was established, you could send comrades on missions to liberated strongholds. With the DLC, you can manage some of these locations directly. You can now lease facilities across Pywel, assign comrades and equipment, choose which goods to sell, and decide how best to run each business to grow its recognition and profits.

New boss challenges

Pearl Abyss said “seasoned fighters seeking a greater test” should consider the new challenge where players face a series of powerful bosses from across Pywel, one after another. If you do well, expect "valuable rewards."

As someone put Crimson Desert down some time ago having sunk over 100 hours into the game, I'm feeling the pull to return to the game for the DLC. Pearl Abyss' relentless pace of updates in the wake of Crimson Desert's launch earlier this year made significant improvements and added game-changing features, but the new systems and mechanics coming with Charting the Unknown clearly take things to a new level. Even if you're not into story side of things, there's plenty to fuss over. The business management system, for example, looks like tens of hours of gameplay alone. Then there's underwater exploration and what I'm sure will end up a fan-favorite: romance.

Crimson Desert Enhanced: Charting the Unknown launches on October 29, 2026 at 2pm PT, 5pm ET, 10pm UK time, on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store.

items.title: 'Aragorn Will Always Be Viggo,' Says Jamie Dornan Ahead of His Turn as the Iconic Character in The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum
items.description: Jamie Dornan will play a younger Aragorn in The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, but he’s aware of the magnitude of his role, and doesn’t see his take on the character as a replacement for Viggo Mortensen.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Jamie Dornan will play a younger Aragorn in The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, but he’s aware of the magnitude of his role, and doesn’t see his take on the character as a replacement for Viggo Mortensen.

"There's pressure when you're trying to follow in those footsteps," Dornan told ScreenRant. "I've been asked to play a super-iconic role, and I'll do my best.

“But for me, Aragorn will always be just Viggo. His performance is one of my all-time favorites, and I feel honored to try to recapture at least some of the energy he originally brought to the character. There's no part of me that's trying to outdo him."

Northern Ireland actor Dornan is best known for his leading role in Fifty Shades of Grey. Viggo Mortensen has already gone on record to back the casting choice, saying he was “thrilled.”

The Hunt for Gollum takes place between The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings and follows Gandalf and Aragorn as they track Sméagol across Middle-earth to find out if a certain magical ring is Sauron's One Ring. The story is summarized in Tolkien’s The Fellowship of the Ring novel, but the movie will build upon those short passages and flesh the journey out into a full story.

Dornan is joined by Leo Woodall (White Lotus, One Day), who will play a fellow Dúnedain Ranger called Halvard joining Strider on his mission. Lee Pace will also return to his Hobbit trilogy role as Thranduil the Elvenking.

Andy Serkis returns as Gollum and also directs the movie, while Sir Ian McKellen and Elijah Wood reprise their classic roles as Gandalf and Frodo respectively. Mortensen previously said he’d only return as Aragorn if he “was right for the character.”

The actor also previously spoke about how he “wasn’t crazy about” the digital de-ageing technology used in The Irishman, which could potentially be a reason he won’t don the cloak and hood again. Of course, we haven’t seen what technology The Hunt for Golem uses to make Elijah Wood and Sir Ian McKellen look younger than they did in the original trilogy yet, with set pictures only showing us a glimpse of Frodo’s back.

Filming began earlier this year, and was teased with photos of Serkis squatting in the motion capture volume, getting his Gollum on. Rather his knees than mine. Elsewhere, Peter Jackson has confirmed The Lord of the Rings: Shadow of the Past is in the scriptwriting stage following cancellation rumors that emerged in the wake of the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.

Photo by Aurore Marechal/Getty Images.

media:description.$text:
WHO'S RUMORED: Aragorn

Previous rumors indicated that a young Aragorn might factor into Amazon's Lord of the Rings series, but unless they're using him as a framing device, we can assume he won't make an appearance. The rumor came from a fan outlet known as The One Ring, which has been reliable in the past, but this one just doesn't check out.

Aragorn was also born well into the Third Age, and though he's lived a life far longer than a normal human (thanks, Dunedain blood!), you can't simply have him appear a couple of thousand years before he was actually alive.

items.title: Fans React to Shrek 2 Remastered's Surprising PC Requirements
items.description: Shrek 2 isn’t exactly pushing the bounds of PC graphics, but the recommended specs for the remaster are surprisingly hefty.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Shrek 2 isn’t exactly pushing the bounds of PC graphics, but the recommended specs for the remaster are surprisingly hefty. Originally released in 2004, this remaster boasts better textures, enhanced UI, 4K resolution — and, it seems, a beefy PC.

According to the Steam page, to even run Shrek 2 Remastered you’ll need a GeForce RTX 4060 or RTX 3060 Ti graphics card or equivalent. The developer recommends a GeForce RTX 4070 or RTX 5070 to get the best experience. What have they been feeding him? Have a look at the screenshots in the slideshow, below, to get a sense of what to expect.

“Those swamp graphics better be baller,” said one X / Twitter user. Another complained that they’re able to run Red Dead Redemption 2 at the highest settings, but their PC would apparently struggle with this makeover of a 22-year-old game.

“Seems a bit much for a remaster of a GameCube game but if that’s what we need to render Shrek’s highly detailed green skin then so be it,” said another Twitter user. “They went full in with the GTA 6 aesthetics,” said another.

Other posts expressed concern over it being a “vibe coded” remaster, but there’s currently no AI disclosure on Steam to suggest that’s the case. Valve asked developers to specify when they use AI during game creation or marketing.

Shrek 2 Remastered was revealed alongside a trailer that parodied GTA 6, and is set to launch just over a week before Rockstar’s behemoth, on November 10. Despite the parody trailer, no one expected it to have similar graphical demands as GTA 6, but here we are. You’ll need 12-16GB of VRAM for this beast. It’s a bit ogre the top.

The remaster is developed by port specialist Aspyr, the studio behind Lord of the Rings: War in the North — Legacy Edition, Deus Ex: Remastered, Tomb Raider 1-3 Remastered, and the disastrous Star Wars: Battlefront Classic Collection.
